claim: Under OOMPolicy=kill the kernel kills the WHOLE scope. The arc's sidecar was written only after pytest returned, by a shell inside that same scope, so a memory-cap OOM during a leg-A run destroyed the verdict: measured arm B of the pressure probe -> SIDECAR=ABSENT, only a 769-byte partial .txt pytest log survived. The Hermes worker scope is exactly this configuration (tools/process_registry.py:273-308: systemd-run --user --scope --property MemoryMax=<n> --property OOMPolicy=kill, 4 GiB measured live), and leg A's own peak is 2.97-3.93 GB of it (91.5% in the heavier sample), so the loss is latent but armed at ~8.5% headroom. Same class of loss SUITE-ISO-2 fixed for the pytest harness (--sink); never checked for the arc.
